questions: Did the weakness develop rapidly over a period of days to weeks, rather than slowly over months to years?
Do you have any family members with similar weakness or a known hereditary neuropathy?
Did you have a respiratory infection or diarrheal illness in the 1–4 weeks before this started?
Is the weakness continuing to get worse?
Have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or sensory loss in your feet or hands?
Do you have difficulty with fine motor tasks such as buttoning shirts, writing, or picking up small objects?
Is there any weakness or asymmetry of the face on the left side as well as the right, even if more subtle?
Do you have any difficulty swallowing, chewing, or speaking, or any change in your voice?
Have you had any shortness of breath or difficulty taking a deep breath?
Have you experienced any double vision, blurred vision, or drooping of the eyelids?
Have you had any vaccinations in the past 4–6 weeks?
Have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder function, such as incontinence or retention?
Have you had any tick exposure or a bull's-eye-shaped rash in the past several months?
Have you had any new or significant pain in your back, neck, or limbs?
Have you ever had similar symptoms before, even if milder?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1H (CMT1H) due to an autosomal dominant heterozygous FBLN5 c.1117C>T (p.Arg373Cys) mutation

Alternatives to consider:
1. Another hereditary demyelinating motor-predominant neuropathy with superimposed unilateral Bell's palsy (coincidental cranial mononeuropathy) — given that CMT1H does not typically cause unilateral facial palsy, the facial asymmetry may represent a coincidental idiopathic facial nerve palsy.
2. A different CMT subtype (e.g., CMT1F or another FBLN5-related variant) with atypical cranial nerve involvement producing the diplopia/ptosis and facial weakness.
3. Hereditary neuralgic amyotrophy / HNPP (PMP22 deletion) presenting with a pressure-related facial palsy on a background of demyelinating NCS — less likely without episodic or pressure-related limb palsies.
